text: Which of the following types of soil have the best bearing capacity?
option1: Clay
option2: Sandy
option3: Gravel
option4: Silty
rationale: Gravel has the highest bearing capacity, followed by sandy soil, clay, and lastly silty soil[cite: 2].

text: What is the purpose of the Environmental Protection Agency's National Priorities List (NPL)?
option1: Identifies hazardous sites that need to be cleaned up through the Superfund program
option2: Identifies endangered species that need to be protected by the federal Endangered Species Act
option3: Identifies pesticides that need to be registered under the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA)
option4: Identifies business operations that emit large quantities of greenhouse gas that is regulated by the Climate Action Plan
rationale: The National Priorities List (NPL) identifies priority hazardous waste sites for cleanup under the Federal Superfund program[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following is NOT one of six principal pollutants identified by EPA in its National Air Quality Standards?
option1: Carbon Dioxide
option2: Nitrogen Dioxide
option3: Sulfur Dioxide
option4: Lead
rationale: The 6 criteria pollutants under NAAQS are Carbon Monoxide, Lead, Nitrogen Dioxide, Ozone, Particle Pollution (PM), and Sulfur Dioxide[cite: 2]. Carbon Dioxide is not one of the six[cite: 2].

text:
What effects do user characteristics have on architectural programming?
A. Favoring some adjacencies over others
B. Altering circulation patterns
C. Affecting the size of program spaces
D. Creating a need for additional program spaces based on needs of culture, age, disability, etc.
option1: A, B and C
option2: A, C and D
option3: B, C and D
option4: All of the above
rationale: User characteristics such as age, accessibility needs, and group dynamics affect all spatial adjacencies, sizing, and circulation requirements[cite: 2].

text: Identify the version of the LEED rating system launched in November 2013:
option1: LEED 2009
option2: LEED 2013
option3: LEED v3
option4: LEED v4
rationale: LEED v4 was introduced in November 2013 at Greenbuild[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following is an effective method you would use to solicit stakeholder input?
option1: Schedule a scoping meeting with the agency having jurisdiction
option2: Hold design charrettes and invite stakeholders to participate
option3: Organize social gathering and invite stakeholders to participate
option4: Publish article in local newspapers describing positive aspects of your project
rationale: Design charrettes are active collaborative workshops specifically designed to elicit community and stakeholder input[cite: 2].

text: Other than using a 'Bubble Diagram' what is another tool for analyzing spatial relationships?
option1: Adjacency Matrix
option2: Relationship Map
option3: Adjacency Chart
option4: Relationship Diagram
rationale: An Adjacency Matrix is the standard architectural tool used alongside bubble diagrams to evaluate relationships[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following is a factor that should typically be considered when estimating the initial project cost of a project during programming phase?
option1: Cost of finish materials
option2: Cost of utilities and infrastructure
option3: Labor cost relative to the geographic location of the project
option4: Escalation
rationale: Escalation accounts for inflation across the multi-year duration of design and construction, making it critical even at the programming stage[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following are projects exempt from the provisions of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)?
option1: In an urbanized area, a construction project with a scope of four single-family units
option2: A garage
option3: A repair to a public service building required for maintaining service
option4: A maintenance project of 2 miles within a public street
rationale: Per CEQA categorical exemptions (Class 3), accessory structures like garages are exempt[cite: 2]. Note: urban single-family exemptions cover up to 3 units, maintenance in streets covers up to 1 mile, and only emergency repairs are exempt[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following is the correct qualification of inspectors for Essential Services Buildings?
option1: Meet the qualification for inspectors as specified by the California Division of State Architect
option2: Meet the qualification for inspectors in the California Building Code
option3: Certified by the International Conference of Building Officials
option4: Certified by the State of California
rationale: Inspectors must be certified by ICBO / ICC according to the Essential Services Buildings Seismic Safety Act[cite: 2].

text:
Besides the structural system what other components of an essential services building are regulated by the Essential Services Building Seismic Safety Act?
A. Communication System
B. Main Transformer
C. Switch Gear
D. Intercom system
E. Emergency backup system
option1: A, B and C
option2: A, B, C and E
option3: B, C, D and E
option4: All of the above
rationale: The Act protects vital operational systems (communication with field emergency units, power transformers, switch gear, emergency backup)[cite: 2]. An internal intercom (D) is not regulated under the Act[cite: 2].

text: Other than the California Green Building Standards Code, what other code or regulation also have provisions concerning sustainability?
option1: California Water Code
option2: California Historical Building Code
option3: California Clean Air Act
option4: Field Act
rationale: The California Historical Building Code (CHBC) expressly includes sustainability principles in its intent section to facilitate reuse and conservation[cite: 2].

text: Per the structural provisions of the California Building Code, which of the following is a load bearing wall?
option1: A wood stud wall that supports more than 50 lbs per lineal foot
option2: A metal stud wall that supports more than 80 lbs per lineal foot
option3: A CMU wall that supports more than 100 lbs per lineal foot
option4: A reinforced concrete wall that supports more than 200 lbs per lineal foot
rationale: A load-bearing wall supports more than 200 lbs per lineal foot of superimposed vertical load[cite: 2].

text: The California Building Code specifies that non-load bearing partitions are to be isolated from the structural system by which of the following?
option1: Compression struts
option2: Slip tracks
option3: Deflection isolators
option4: Flex clips
rationale: Slip tracks accommodate structural floor/roof deflection without imposing vertical loads onto interior partitions[cite: 2].

text: Provisions for which of the following building functions or building components are included in Chapter 11B of the California Building Code?
option1: Mechanical Access Parking Garage
option2: Teletypewriter (TTY)
option3: Electric Vehicle Charging Station (EVCS)
option4: Destination-oriented Elevator
rationale: Section 11B-228 of the CBC contains extensive California-specific standards for Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS)[cite: 2].

text: According to the California Building Code when you have two exit stairs required to be separated by at least half the floor diagonal, how is this distance measured?
option1: From the center point of the doorway of the stair enclosure to the center point of the doorway of the other stair enclosure
option2: From any point along the doorway of the stair enclosure to any point along the doorway of the other stair enclosure
option3: From the center point of the first riser of the exit access stairway to the center point of the first riser of the other exit access stairway
option4: The distance between the closest risers of the exit access stairways
rationale: For exit access stairways, measurement is taken between the closest risers of the respective stairs[cite: 2].

text: A third exit stair is required for which of the following?
option1: A high-rise building with occupied floors above the height of 120 ft.
option2: A high-rise building with occupied floors above the height of 240 ft.
option3: A high-rise building with occupied floors above the height of 420 ft.
option4: A high-rise building with occupied floors above the height of 600 ft.
rationale: CBC Section 403 requires buildings with occupied floors greater than 420 feet in height to provide an additional exit stairway[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following is NOT regulated by the California Energy Code (Title 24 Part 6)?
option1: Indoor lighting systems
option2: Outdoor lighting systems
option3: Signs located either indoors or outdoors
option4: None of the above, they are all regulated
rationale: All three categories (indoor lighting, outdoor lighting, and signs) are strictly regulated under the California Energy Code[cite: 2].

text: According to the Retail Food Code, floor drains are required in food facilities with which of the following conditions?
option1: In areas where the floors are water-flushed for cleaning
option2: In areas with ceramic tile floors
option3: In lieu of a grease trap
option4: In areas where the floor surfaces are less than 1:50 in slope
rationale: Floor drains are required in food preparation facilities where floors are cleaned by water-flushing[cite: 2].

text:
Which of the following are required to file a Preliminary 20-Day Notice in order to preserve their right to record a Mechanic's Lien?
A. Prime Contractor
B. Sub-Contractor
C. Material Supplier
D. Architect (Direct Contract)
option1: A and B
option2: B and C
option3: A, B and C
option4: All of the above
rationale: Claimants without direct contractual relationships to the owner (subcontractors and material suppliers) must serve a Preliminary 20-Day Notice[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following are required by the California Hospital Facilities Seismic Safety Act to meet seismic standards?
option1: All new acute care in-patient hospitals
option2: All acute care in-patient hospitals (new and existing)
option3: All acute care in-patient hospitals constructed prior to 1994
option4: All acute care in-patient hospitals more than 2 stories and other than type V construction
rationale: The Alfred E. Alquist Hospital Facilities Seismic Safety Act applies to all acute care in-patient hospitals, requiring both new and existing structures to comply[cite: 2].

text: The Field Act applies to which of the following?
option1: All public schools except charter schools
option2: All public schools
option3: All public schools and community colleges
option4: All public schools, community colleges, University of California and California State University buildings
rationale: The Field Act covers public elementary and secondary schools (K-12) and community colleges under DSA jurisdiction[cite: 2]. (UC/CSU are not subject to the Field Act)[cite: 2].

text: The Architects Practice Act requires licensees to report to the California Architects Board any civil action judgments, settlements, or arbitration awards of which amount?
option1: $1,000 or greater
option2: $2,000 or greater
option3: $5,000 or greater
option4: $10,000 or greater
rationale: B&P Code § 5588 requires reporting settlements or judgments of $5,000 or greater within 30 days[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following is a condition where the Architect is NOT required to have a written contract with the Client?
option1: The Architect is designing a townhouse in a development he had designed an identical townhouse for the mother of his client
option2: The Architect is designing a post office for the US Postal Service which he had designed a similar post office for elsewhere
option3: The Architect is designing a fast food restaurant for a national chain which he had designed a storage facility for previously
option4: The Architect is designing a chain retail store in a mall for a national chain which he had designed an identical store for previously
rationale: B&P Code § 5536.22 exempts architectural services of the same general kind which the architect has previously rendered to and received payment from the same client[cite: 2].

text: According to the Architects Practice Act, which of the following actions by an unlicensed individual qualifies as practicing architecture without a license?
option1: Use a stamp that bears the legend 'Building Designer'
option2: Make claim on a resume of having many years of architectural experience
option3: Tell a friend that he/she is an architect
option4: Distribute business cards that bear the title 'Architectural Designer'
rationale: Using professional-style stamps or holding out as an architect/building designer in commercial practice is prohibited[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following represents the exempt residential project under the California Architects Practice Act?
option1: Multiple dwellings with no more than 4 dwelling units of wood frame construction, not more than 2 stories and a basement in height
option2: Multiple dwellings with no more than 3 dwelling units of wood frame construction, not more than 2 stories and a basement in height
option3: Multiple dwellings with no more than 4 dwelling units of wood frame construction, not more than 3 stories and a basement in height
option4: Multiple dwellings with no more than 3 dwelling units of wood frame construction, not more than 3 stories and a basement in height
rationale: B&P Code § 5537 exempts multi-family dwellings of no more than 4 units of wood frame construction, not more than 2 stories and basement[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following is NOT a rule of professional conduct in the California Code of Regulations Title 16?
option1: An architect shall only accept work that he/she is qualified to perform by education, training, and experience
option2: An architect shall exercise responsible control when practicing architecture
option3: In designing a project, an architect shall have knowledge of all applicable building laws, codes, and regulations
option4: Whenever the Board is conducting an investigation, an architect is required to respond within 30 days
rationale: The standard of care rule states an architect shall exercise reasonable skill and care[cite: 2]. 'Responsible control' is a statutory definition for sealing documents, not phrased as this conduct rule[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following acts governs professional corporations in California?
option1: Brown Reagan Professional Corporation Act
option2: Deukmejian Wilson Professional Corporation Act
option3: Davis Schwarzenegger Professional Corporation Act
option4: Moscone Knox Professional Corporation Act
rationale: The Moscone-Knox Professional Corporation Act (CA Corp Code § 13400) governs professional corporations[cite: 2].

text: Variances are typically granted for properties to allow for which of the following?
option1: Special uses not enjoyed by nearby, similarly zoned land
option2: The sub-division of a property
option3: The development of a property beyond the strict physical requirements of zoning regulations
option4: Relaxation of design guidelines that supplements zoning control
rationale: A variance allows waiver of physical development standards (setbacks, height, FAR) due to site hardship, but NEVER allows a use variance in California[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following is true of the accessibility provisions of the California Building Code and the ADA Standards?
option1: The 2 documents are exactly the same
option2: The 2 documents are different because the state amended provisions to make many requirements more stringent
option3: The 2 documents are different because the state excluded housing
option4: The state never adopted ADA guidelines
rationale: Meeting CBC Chapter 11B satisfies ADA, but meeting federal ADA alone does not ensure California compliance, as CBC contains more stringent requirements[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following is the document issued by the FAA in response to proposed developments adjacent to airport facilities?
option1: Aviation Advisory Circular
option2: Letter of Permission
option3: Non-Obstruction Permit
option4: Airspace Determination
rationale: Advisory Circulars and official determinations address obstructions to navigable airspace[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following is the environmental study document required per the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA)?
option1: Environmental Impact Study
option2: Environmental Impact Statement (EIS)
option3: Environmental Impact Survey
option4: Environmental Impact Summary
rationale: Under federal NEPA, an Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) is prepared (as opposed to an EIR under California CEQA)[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following is an organization that develops consensus standards for construction materials and systems?
option1: Underwriters Laboratories (UL)
option2: Factory Mutual (FM)
option3: American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM)
option4: Warnock Hersey (WH)
rationale: ASTM develops material and test standards; UL and Warnock Hersey are primarily testing and certifying laboratories[cite: 2].

text: AISC 360 is a national design standard for which of the following?
option1: Wood
option2: Concrete
option3: Masonry
option4: Steel
rationale: AISC is the American Institute of Steel Construction[cite: 2].

text: Which local agency is designated as a California Certified Unified Program Agency (CUPA)?
option1: Local Building Department
option2: Local Fire Department
option3: Local Public Works Department
option4: Local Environmental Health Department
rationale: Local Fire Departments (or Environmental Health Departments in some counties) serve as the CUPA for hazardous materials programs[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following is NOT a responsibility of Regional Water Quality Control Boards (RWQCB)?
option1: Certifies operators of wastewater treatment facilities
option2: Prescribe Waste Discharge Requirements (WDRs) for each discharge of waste
option3: Cleanup unauthorized discharges into groundwater under Site Clean-Up Program
option4: Implement BMPs to control pollutants in stormwater
rationale: Operator certification is handled at the State Water Resources Control Board level, not the Regional Boards[cite: 2].

text: In addition to the San Francisco Bay Conservation and Development Commission, which of the following regions has a regional planning authority?
option1: Death Valley
option2: Yosemite
option3: Lake Tahoe Basin
option4: Big Sur
rationale: The Tahoe Regional Planning Agency (TRPA) is a bi-state regional environmental planning authority[cite: 2].

text: The Water Resources Control Board protects water quality by administering programs for which of the following?
option1: Toxic Cleanup, Waste Disposal, and Storm Water
option2: Toxic Cleanup, Waste Disposal, and Recycling
option3: Toxic Cleanup, Storm Water, and Recycling
option4: All of the above
rationale: The SWRCB regulates toxic cleanup, waste disposal, stormwater permits, and water recycling[cite: 2].

text: Which federal agency is NOT under the jurisdiction of the GSA and permits its own building construction projects?
option1: Environmental Protection Agency
option2: Department of Housing and Urban Development
option3: Federal Courts System
option4: Veterans Affairs Administration
rationale: The VA has independent statutory authority to design, permit, and construct its own facilities[cite: 2].

text: A Standard Permit issued by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is for which of the following?
option1: Projects approved on an accelerated timeline
option2: Projects with more than minimal individual or cumulative impact on aquatic resources
option3: Projects with minimal impact on aquatic resources
option4: Projects with no impact on aquatic resources
rationale: Standard Individual Permits are required for projects that cause more than minimal impacts on waters of the US (as opposed to Nationwide / General Permits)[cite: 2].

text: During the CEQA process, how is the Lead Agency determined when multiple public agencies are involved?
option1: Typically, the agency that provides utility services
option2: Typically, the agency with a single regulatory purpose
option3: Typically, the agency with general governmental powers such as a city or a county
option4: The Owner selects the lead agency
rationale: Under CEQA Guidelines § 15051, the agency with broader governmental powers (such as a city or county) acts as the Lead Agency[cite: 2].

text: Which agency is responsible for providing CEQA implementation guidelines and operating the State Clearinghouse?
option1: California State Clearing Board
option2: Environmental Review Coordination Board
option3: California Unified Program Agency
option4: Governor's Office of Planning and Research (OPR)
rationale: OPR develops CEQA guidelines and operates the State Clearinghouse for state-level environmental review[cite: 2].

text: Typically what happens when there are conflicting requirements between different applicable codes and regulations?
option1: The more restrictive applies
option2: The agency having jurisdiction will decide
option3: Architect can choose
option4: The less restrictive applies
rationale: Standard code hierarchy principles state that where conflicts occur, the most restrictive requirement governs[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following is a responsibility of the civil engineer during Schematic Design?
option1: Prepare boundary surveys
option2: Prepare preliminary parking layouts
option3: Prepare preliminary irrigation plans
option4: Prepare stormwater pollution prevention plans
rationale: Civil engineers develop preliminary stormwater drainage and SWPPP strategies; boundary surveys are provided by the Owner's surveyor[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following consultants typically produces drawings for municipal planning review?
option1: Landscape Architect
option2: Acoustical Engineer
option3: Structural Engineer
option4: Lighting Designer
rationale: Landscape architects prepare site landscape and planting schemes, which are standard submittals for Planning / Design Review Boards[cite: 2].

text: The Owner has provided you with the scope, budget, and schedule. What additional item do you need to begin Schematic Design?
option1: Geotechnical engineer report
option2: Tests, inspections, and reports required by law
option3: Site survey
option4: Information in regards to lien rights
rationale: A verified site boundary and topographic survey is necessary to orient and configure the building footprint during SD[cite: 2].

text: What does your local planning department do after a date has been set for your presentation to the Planning Commission?
option1: Issue a Notice of Preparation
option2: Notify owners and residents within a specified radius of the project site so they can comment
option3: Notify all responsible agencies to solicit comments
option4: Submit your project to the state OPR
rationale: Public hearing notices are mailed to surrounding property owners and occupants (typically within a 300 to 500-foot radius)[cite: 2].

text: Typically when is a project submitted to the planning department for design and environmental review?
option1: Schematic Design Phase
option2: Design Development Phase
option3: Construction Document Phase
option4: Bid and Negotiation Phase
rationale: Planning entitlements and environmental reviews are best submitted during Schematic Design before spending substantial fees detailing in DD or CD[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following milestones are recommended times to exchange progress sets with consultants for interdisciplinary coordination?
option1: 90% SD, 50% DD, 90% DD, 50% CD and 90% CD
option2: 50% DD, 90% DD, 50% CD, 75% CD and 90% CD
option3: 50% DD, 90% DD, 50% CD and 90% CD
option4: 90% DD, 50% CD and 90% CD
rationale: 50% DD, 90% DD, 50% CD, and 90% CD provide balanced coordination gates across design development and construction documents[cite: 2].

text:
Which of the following are methods that architectural firms typically use in their quality control process?
A. The use of Project Checklists
B. The use of updated Standard Details
C. The use of Masterspec
option1: A
option2: B
option3: A and B
option4: All of the above
rationale: Checklists and office standard details are internal QC systems[cite: 2]. Masterspec is simply a third-party starting master; it does not in itself constitute firm QA/QC[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following is the best thing that an Architect can do to address the issue of Standard of Care with the client?
option1: Explain that the architect cannot be expected to do a perfect job
option2: Include a contractual definition of standard of care
option3: Have the client include contingencies in his/her budget
option4: Obtain Professional Liability Insurance
rationale: Educating the client to maintain realistic design/construction contingencies aligns expectations with the legal reality that perfection is not required[cite: 2].

text: Your client wants significant amounts of glazing for a panoramic view house. What structural framing system is most appropriate?
option1: Steel Frame
option2: Timber Frame (Heavy Timber)
option3: Platform Frame
option4: Balloon Frame
rationale: Heavy timber/post-and-beam allows wide spans and large unobstructed glazed openings without the prohibitive cost of structural steel[cite: 2].

text: According to CALGreen (Title 24 Part 11), what document is required to be submitted for permit?
option1: Construction Debris Recycle Program
option2: Energy Management Plan
option3: Water Consumption Program
option4: Construction Waste Management Plan
rationale: CALGreen requires a Construction Waste Management Plan documenting diversion of at least 65% of nonhazardous C&D waste[cite: 2].

text: According to CBC Chapter 17, what is required to be submitted to the building official for permit application?
option1: Reports of Structural Integrity
option2: Statement of Special Inspections prepared by the registered design professional
option3: Structural Calculations only
option4: Soils reports only
rationale: Chapter 17 requires the design professional in responsible charge to prepare and submit a Statement of Special Inspections[cite: 2].

text: A 'trapeze' hanger system is typically used to support and seismic-brace which of the following?
option1: Piping and conduits
option2: Suspended lighting fixtures
option3: Tall bookcases
option4: Photovoltaics on rooftops
rationale: Trapeze hangers (unistrut with threaded rods) support horizontal conduits, ducts, and pipe runs[cite: 2].

text: Which lateral force-resisting system resists shear forces primarily through axial tension and compression?
option1: Braced Frame
option2: Moment Frame
option3: Space Frame
option4: Waffle Slab
rationale: Braced frames resist lateral loads through axial tension and compression in diagonal members[cite: 2].

text:
Which of the following are recognized categories of automated building energy management controls?
A. Energy Optimization Systems
B. Time-of-day Scheduling Systems
C. Temperature/Time Optimization Systems
D. Demand Control Systems
option1: A, B and C
option2: A, B and D
option3: A, C and D
option4: B, C and D
rationale: Time scheduling, setback optimization, and demand control ventilation/load shedding are standard energy management techniques[cite: 2].

text: According to passive thermal zoning principles, internal heat-generating 'hot zones' (such as commercial kitchens) should ideally be located along which exposure?
option1: North
option2: East
option3: South
option4: West
rationale: Placing internal heat-generating spaces on the north (cool) side reduces overall cooling loads by avoiding additional solar heat gain[cite: 2].

text: Under CSI MasterFormat, in which division are clock and program systems specified?
option1: 10 00 00 - Specialties
option2: 11 00 00 - Equipment
option3: 12 00 00 - Furnishings
option4: 13 00 00 - Special Construction
rationale: Clock systems and signages fall under Division 10 (Specialties)[cite: 2].

text: Cost estimates show a project on budget, but the Owner has strict funding and insists on a guarantee that contractor bids will not exceed budget. What should you do?
option1: Agree to guarantee only for an additional fee
option2: Tell the Owner to carry contingencies through bidding
option3: Explain that architects cannot guarantee bids, and help identify additive/deductive bid alternates
option4: Lower unit cost estimates
rationale: Architects cannot guarantee bids because they do not control contractor market pricing[cite: 2]. Incorporating bid alternates gives the owner budget flexibility[cite: 2].

text: Public works projects in California are required to be advertised for bids in newspapers/trade publications in which manner?
option1: Twice a week for at least 1 week
option2: Once a week for at least 2 weeks
option3: Twice a week for at least 2 weeks
option4: Once a week for at least 3 weeks
rationale: California Public Contract Code requires notice inviting bids published once a week for at least two consecutive weeks[cite: 2].

text:
Which of the following must the Owner furnish to the Contractor under AIA A201?
A. Financial information regarding lien rights
B. Legal description and site survey
C. Special inspection and testing services
option1: A and B
option2: B and C
option3: A, B and C
option4: A, B and D
rationale: Under A201 and California codes, the Owner provides site surveys, financial evidence, and directly contracts independent testing/special inspection agencies[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following architectural actions constitutes an official interpretation of the Contract Documents?
option1: Responding to Requests for Information (RFIs)
option2: Issuing Architect's Supplemental Instructions (ASIs)
option3: Issuing Work Change Proposal Requests
option4: All of the above
rationale: Responding to an RFI interprets the existing drawings/specifications[cite: 2]. ASIs order minor changes, and proposal requests initiate potential changes[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following is true regarding mediation versus arbitration?
option1: Mediation is non-binding
option2: Arbitration is non-binding
option3: Both are non-binding
option4: Both are binding
rationale: Mediation is a non-binding facilitated negotiation[cite: 2]. Arbitration results in a final, legally binding award[cite: 2].

text: Under what circumstance will an Architect issue an Architect's Supplemental Instruction (ASI)?
option1: To order a minor change in the work not involving adjustment in Contract Sum or Contract Time
option2: To provide the Contractor with instructions on means and methods
option3: To supplement information after a Construction Change Directive has been issued
option4: To supersede local code approvals
rationale: AIA Document G710 (ASI) is used to direct minor changes in the work that do not alter contract sum or time[cite: 2].

text: If the Architect discovers evidence that the work cannot be completed for the unpaid contract balance, per AIA A201 the Architect has the right to do what?
option1: Recommend that Owner terminate Contract immediately
option2: Suggest Owner hire another contractor to complete work
option3: Nullify or withhold the whole or part of a Certificate for Payment
option4: File an immediate mechanic's lien on behalf of the owner
rationale: A201 § 9.5 allows the architect to withhold or nullify a Certificate for Payment to protect the owner from loss[cite: 2].

text: What is the Contractor's responsibility regarding special inspections during construction?
option1: Submit statement of special inspection to the building official
option2: Employ and pay special inspectors directly
option3: File weekly inspector reports to DSA
option4: Provide access and keep records of all special inspections on the job site
rationale: The owner contracts the special inspector, while the contractor coordinates access and keeps copies of records on site[cite: 2].

text: When conducting an inspection for a Certificate of Occupancy, which of the following is NOT an inspection item for the Fire Marshal?
option1: Fire rated doors and hardware
option2: Posted occupancy load signage
option3: Lighting occupancy sensors
option4: Fire alarms and strobes
rationale: Lighting occupancy sensors are an Energy Code (Title 24 Part 6) / electrical inspection item, not life-safety within the Fire Marshal's scope[cite: 2].

text: Which of the following does NOT happen at Substantial Completion?
option1: Owner assumes responsibility for security, utilities, and insurance
option2: Contractor submits Consent of Surety for final payment
option3: Notice of Completion can be recorded by the Owner
option4: Warranties and punch lists commence
rationale: Consent of Surety (AIA G707) is submitted at Final Payment / Final Completion, not at Substantial Completion[cite: 2].

text: What is the California Statute of Limitations for bringing legal action against design professionals for patent (visible/apparent) construction defects?
option1: 4 years
option2: 8 years
option3: 10 years
option4: No statute of limitations
rationale: California Code of Civil Procedure § 337.1 establishes a 4-year statute of limitations for patent defects (latent defects have a 10-year limit under § 337.15)[cite: 2].

text: The term 'Zone of Intermittent Saturation' refers to which of the following?
option1: The watershed of a seasonal stream or creek
option2: The part of a wetland area that serves as storage for storm water runoff
option3: The subsurface area between the level of summer and winter water table
option4: The subsurface area from grade level to the water table
rationale: The zone of intermittent saturation is the subsurface soil layer between the lowest seasonal water table (dry/summer) and highest water table (wet/winter)[cite: 1].

text: What is soil liquefaction?
option1: The mixing of saturated cohesionless sand or soil that loses shear strength during earthquake ground shaking
option2: The loosening of top soil during heavy rain
option3: The erosion of bedrock due to capillary action of subsurface drainage
option4: The contamination of underground aquifers by hazardous materials
rationale: Liquefaction occurs when loose, saturated granular soils lose strength and stiffness due to increased pore water pressure during seismic shaking[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following is a naturally occurring radioactive indoor air pollutant?
option1: Lead
option2: Formaldehyde
option3: Radon
option4: Asbestos
rationale: Radon is an odorless, naturally occurring radioactive gas produced by the radioactive decay of uranium in soil and rock[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following is an effective method to ensure ongoing user involvement in an architectural project?
option1: Form a steering committee with representatives from key user groups
option2: Keep users informed by giving presentations at every project milestone
option3: Conduct one-time user surveys
option4: Organize social gatherings and invite users
rationale: Forming a steering committee with representatives from key user groups provides active, continuous participation in decision-making[cite: 1].

text:
Which of the following are recognized methods an architect can use to uncover stakeholder expectations?
A. Charrettes
B. Focus Groups
C. Opinion surveys
D. Direct Observations
option1: A, B and C
option2: A, C and D
option3: B, C and D
option4: All of the above
rationale: Different stakeholder groups respond to different discovery methods; charrettes, focus groups, surveys, and site observations are all effective[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following is NOT a recognized LEED professional credential awarded by GBCI?
option1: LEED Green Associate
option2: LEED Authorized Professional
option3: LEED Commissioning Engineer
option4: LEED Fellow
rationale: LEED Commissioning Engineer is not a GBCI credential[cite: 1]. Recognized credentials are LEED GA, LEED AP (with specialty), and LEED Fellow[cite: 1].

text:
In addition to adjacency, what other spatial relationships can typically be shown in Bubble Diagrams?
A. Circulation connections between spaces
B. Spaces that require acoustic privacy
C. Spaces that require future flexibility
D. Spaces that require physical separation with intervening buffers
option1: A, B and C
option2: A, B and D
option3: B, C and D
option4: All of the above
rationale: Circulation paths, acoustic separation, and physical barriers can be drawn graphically[cite: 1]. Flexibility is programmatic and difficult to represent in a bubble diagram[cite: 1].

text: When putting together a feasibility study for a retail shopping mall, which of the following is the most critical factor that determines economic viability?
option1: Zoning regulations
option2: Construction cost
option3: Infrastructure
option4: Demographics
rationale: For commercial retail projects, surrounding demographics and buying power dictate whether sufficient customer volume exists to support the center[cite: 1].

text: Identify the correct sequential workflow of CEQA environmental documentation:
option1: Initial Study -> Notice of Determination -> Notice of Exemption -> Negative Declaration
option2: Notice of Exemption (if applicable) -> Initial Study -> Negative Declaration -> Notice of Determination
option3: Notice of Determination -> Initial Study -> Negative Declaration -> Notice of Exemption
option4: Initial Study -> Notice of Exemption -> Notice of Determination -> Negative Declaration
rationale: The lead agency first determines if an exemption applies (NOE)[cite: 1]. If not exempt, it conducts an Initial Study; if no significant impacts, it drafts a Neg Dec, and finally files a Notice of Determination (NOD)[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following is classified as an Essential Services Building under California law?
option1: A California Highway Patrol Station
option2: A general acute hospital
option3: A public high school
option4: A regional office of FEMA
rationale: Under the Essential Services Buildings Seismic Safety Act, CHP stations, fire stations, police stations, and emergency operations centers are included[cite: 1]. (Hospitals are governed by OSHPD/HCAI; FEMA is federal)[cite: 1].

text: According to the California Building Code, what is the minimum floor area requirement for an Efficiency Dwelling Unit?
option1: 220 sq. ft.
option2: 240 sq. ft.
option3: 300 sq. ft.
option4: 320 sq. ft.
rationale: CBC Section 1208 requires efficiency dwelling units to have a living room of not less than 220 sq. ft.[cite: 1] (or 150 sq. ft. in specific jurisdictions adopting local micro-unit amendments).

text: According to the California Building Code, what is the minimum size requirement for a Fire Service Access Elevator (FSAE) lobby?
option1: 120 sq. ft. in size and 8 ft. minimum each side
option2: 120 sq. ft. in size and 10 ft. minimum each side
option3: 150 sq. ft. in size and 8 ft. minimum dimension
option4: 150 sq. ft. in size and 10 ft. minimum dimension
rationale: CBC Section 3007 specifies the FSAE lobby must be not less than 150 sq. ft. with a minimum dimension of 8 feet[cite: 1].

text: As per the structural requirements of the California Building Code, Risk Category (Occupancy Category) IV includes which structures?
option1: Buildings and structures designated as essential facilities
option2: Buildings that represent a substantial hazard to human life in event of failure
option3: Buildings that represent a moderate hazard to human life
option4: Buildings that represent a low hazard to human life
rationale: Category IV structures are designated essential facilities (police, fire, emergency communications, designated disaster shelters)[cite: 1].

text: According to CBC Chapter 11B, in a multi-compartment restroom, an additional 36-inch wide ambulatory accessible stall is required under which condition?
option1: For every 8 water closets
option2: For every 8 fixtures including combinations of urinals and water closets
option3: For every 6 water closets
option4: Where 6 or more water closets and urinals are provided in the room
rationale: CBC 11B-213.3.1 requires an ambulatory accessible compartment when six or more water closets and urinals combined are installed[cite: 1].

text: What is the ratio requirement for van-accessible parking spaces under CBC Chapter 11B?
option1: At least one for every 5 or fraction of 5 accessible spaces
option2: At least one for every 6 or fraction of 6 accessible spaces
option3: At least one for every 7 or fraction of 7 accessible spaces
option4: At least one for every 8 or fraction of 8 accessible spaces
rationale: CBC 11B-208.2.4 mandates that for every six or fraction of six accessible spaces, at least one must be a van-accessible space[cite: 1] (132" wide stall or 108" stall with 96" aisle).

text: For temporary or movable equipment stationed in one place for no more than 8 hours, current code allows enforcing agencies to require seismic restraints when the equipment exceeds what weight?
option1: 100 lbs
option2: 200 lbs
option3: 300 lbs
option4: 400 lbs
rationale: Equipment weighing more than 400 lbs must be anchored to prevent overturning and slide hazards[cite: 1].

text: The California Electrical Code allows which professional other than registered electrical engineers to serve as Design Reviewers for electrical systems?
option1: Architect
option2: Owner Employed Special Inspector
option3: Building Department Plan Checker
option4: Only electrical engineers
rationale: Licensed architects are recognized as registered design professionals capable of overall system design review[cite: 1].

text: According to the California Health and Safety Code, which of the following safety features is required for all commercial and public swimming pools?
option1: Underwater wet-niche light fixtures
option2: Variable speed circulation pumps
option3: Anti-vortex drains
option4: Anti-entrapment drain covers/devices
rationale: Anti-entrapment covers complying with ASME/ANSI A112.19.8 (or suction limitation systems) are mandated under the Swimming Pool Safety Act[cite: 1].

text: California Design Professional Lien law requires that prior to recording a lien, design professionals must provide the owner with written demand at least how many days in advance?
option1: 10 days
option2: 15 days
option3: 30 days
option4: 60 days
rationale: California Civil Code § 8416 requires design professionals to give the property owner at least 10 days written notice before recording a lien[cite: 1].

text: In order to preserve the right to file a mechanic's lien, when must a sub-contractor serve the Preliminary 20-Day Notice?
option1: Within 20 days after starting construction on the job site
option2: Within 20 days after the subcontractor begins providing work or materials
option3: Within 20 days after completing work
option4: Within 20 days of the first progress payment application
rationale: Civil Code § 8204 states the preliminary notice must be served not later than 20 days after the claimant first furnishes work, services, or equipment[cite: 1].

text: According to the California Clean Air Act, stationary equipment or industrial processes that emit pollutants are required to obtain what from the local AQMD?
option1: Letter of Permission
option2: Permit to Operate (PTO)
option3: General Permit
option4: Standard Permit
rationale: Local Air Quality Management Districts issue an Authority to Construct followed by a Permit to Operate (PTO)[cite: 1].

text: According to the California Coastal Act, what is the general geographic boundary of the Coastal Zone?
option1: Between the sea and the first public road
option2: Extends 1 mile seaward and 1,000 yards inland
option3: Extends seaward 3 miles and 100 yards inland
option4: Extends seaward to state jurisdictional limits (3 nmi) and generally 1,000 yards inland (up to 5 miles in rural habitat/mountain zones)
rationale: The Coastal Zone extends 3 miles offshore to the state boundary and inland generally 1,000 yards, expanding up to 5 miles in undeveloped coastal ridgelines[cite: 1].

text:
Which of the following are required of architects when exercising Responsible Control under California law?
A. Be licensed in California
B. Stamp and sign drawings
C. Exercise standard of care over document preparation
D. Execute a written contract
E. Carry errors and omissions insurance
option1: A and B
option2: A, B and C
option3: A, B, C and D
option4: All of the above
rationale: B&P Code § 5535.1 defines responsible control by licensure, stamp/seal, and direct control and review[cite: 1]. Contracts and insurance are business requirements, not components of responsible control[cite: 1].

text: Under the Architects Practice Act, in which of the following scenarios is the Architect REQUIRED to have a written contract?
option1: Performing pro bono work with zero compensation
option2: Providing services of the same kind previously rendered to and paid for by the same client
option3: Providing architectural services to a professional traffic engineer
option4: The client states in writing that they do not want a contract
rationale: B&P Code § 5536.22 exempts work for professional engineers, but a traffic engineer or unlicensed consultant is not a registered civil/structural/mechanical/electrical engineer[cite: 1].

text: The California Architects Practice Act states that misdemeanor practice of architecture without a license is punishable by what?
option1: Fine of $100 to $2,000 or up to 1 year imprisonment
option2: Fine of $100 to $5,000 or imprisonment in county jail up to 1 year, or both
option3: Fine of $200 to $2,000 or up to 2 years imprisonment
option4: Fine of $200 to $5,000 or up to 2 years imprisonment
rationale: B&P Code § 5536 makes unlicensed practice a misdemeanor punishable by a fine not less than $100 and not more than $5,000, or by imprisonment up to 1 year, or both[cite: 1].

text: Which project is exempt from the licensing provisions of the California Architects Practice Act?
option1: Single-family dwelling of reinforced masonry construction, 2 stories high
option2: Multiple dwellings with 5 wood-frame units, 2 stories high
option3: Clusters of multi-family dwellings totaling 4 units
option4: Garages and similar wood-frame outbuildings not over 2 stories and basement
rationale: Wood frame conventional construction garages, outbuildings, and single-family dwellings are exempt under B&P Code § 5537[cite: 1] (masonry construction requires an architect or engineer).

text: Which of the following is NOT a rule of professional conduct in the California Code of Regulations Title 16?
option1: An architect shall only accept work that he/she is qualified to perform by education, training, and experience
option2: An architect shall exercise responsible control when practicing architecture
option3: In designing a project, an architect shall have knowledge of all applicable building laws, codes, and regulations
option4: Whenever the Board is conducting an investigation, an architect is required to respond within 30 days
rationale: The standard of care rule states an architect shall exercise reasonable skill and care[cite: 1]. 'Responsible control' is a statutory definition for sealing documents, not phrased as this conduct rule[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following acts governs professional corporations in California?
option1: Brown Reagan Professional Corporation Act
option2: Deukmejian Wilson Professional Corporation Act
option3: Davis Schwarzenegger Professional Corporation Act
option4: Moscone Knox Professional Corporation Act
rationale: The Moscone-Knox Professional Corporation Act (CA Corp Code § 13400) governs professional corporations[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following is one of the mandatory elements of a California General Plan?
option1: Sustainability
option2: Noise
option3: Recreation
option4: Public Transit
rationale: The seven mandatory General Plan elements are Land Use, Circulation, Housing, Conservation, Open Space, Noise, and Safety[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following is NOT true regarding private Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions (CC&Rs)?
option1: They are enforced by homeowners associations or private lawsuits
option2: They run with the land to bind future owners
option3: They govern only physical characteristics of properties such as size, roof color, and landscaping
option4: They are recorded with the county recorder
rationale: CC&Rs frequently govern non-physical items such as pet restrictions, rental limitations, quiet hours, and business uses[cite: 1].

text: Who has legal authority to enforce the federal Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) in California?
option1: Local Building Departments
option2: Division of the State Architect (DSA)
option3: OSHPD / HCAI
option4: U.S. Department of Justice or private parties via civil lawsuits
rationale: ADA is a federal civil rights statute enforced by the US Department of Justice and federal courts[cite: 1]. Local building departments enforce Title 24, not the ADA[cite: 1].

text: Which is an area where California Building Code accessibility standards differ and are more stringent than the 2010 ADA Guidelines?
option1: Detectable warning truncated domes at transit boarding and curb ramps
option2: Dimensions of elevator cars
option3: Passenger Loading zones
option4: There are no differences
rationale: California mandates yellow detectable warning truncated domes at curb ramps and hazardous vehicular ways, whereas ADA eliminated some of these requirements[cite: 1].

text: Under federal aviation regulations, when must an architect/sponsor notify the FAA (Form 7460-1)?
option1: Highways taller than 100 ft
option2: Any construction exceeding 100 ft above ground level
option3: Any construction exceeding 200 ft above ground level or within airport approach slope surfaces
option4: Alterations within set distances from a heliport only
rationale: FAA notification is required for structures greater than 200 feet above ground level or piercing imaginary approach surfaces[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following is NOT a federal statute granting the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers regulatory jurisdiction over waters and wetlands?
option1: Rivers and Harbors Act § 10
option2: National Environmental Quality Act
option3: Clean Water Act § 404
option4: Marine Protection, Research and Sanctuaries Act
rationale: There is no 'National Environmental Quality Act' (it is NEPA)[cite: 1]. The Rivers and Harbors Act and Clean Water Act are the Army Corps' statutes[cite: 1].

text: AF&PA / NDS is the recognized national design standard for which building material?
option1: Wood
option2: Concrete
option3: Masonry
option4: Structural Steel
rationale: NDS is the National Design Specification for Wood Construction (American Forest & Paper Association / American Wood Council)[cite: 1].

text: Under the California Unified Program, which local agency typically conducts review and approval of Hazardous Materials Management Plans (HMMP)?
option1: Public Works Department
option2: Department of Environmental Health
option3: Building Department
option4: Local Fire Department
rationale: Local fire departments act as the CUPA to review HMMPs and chemical inventory hazardous materials disclosure[cite: 1].

text:
Which building elements are typically submitted to local police departments for Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) review?
A. Security cameras
B. Alarm systems
C. Access control gates
D. Walk-up ATM machines
option1: A, B and C
option2: A, B and D
option3: B, C and D
option4: All of the above
rationale: Police departments review security site plans including lighting, ATM sightlines, alarms, and electronic access gates[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following is NOT an operational responsibility of county Flood Control Districts?
option1: Protection of watercourses and water conveyance
option2: Protection of land and structures from stormwater flooding
option3: Remediation of underground chemical aquifer contamination
option4: Preservation of floodwater for percolation and beneficial reuse
rationale: Contamination cleanups are handled by the RWQCB and DTSC, not county flood control agencies[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following is NOT a regulatory function of the California Air Resources Board (CARB)?
option1: Regulating formaldehyde emissions from plastic pipe products
option2: Controlling VOC emissions from architectural coatings and paints
option3: Reducing mobile emission sources from freight transport
option4: Developing state clean air implementation plans
rationale: CARB ATCM limits formaldehyde in composite wood products (MDF, particleboard, hardwood plywood), not plastic plumbing pipes[cite: 1].

text:
The California Division of the State Architect (DSA) has full plan check and building enforcement authority over which facility types?
A. K-12 public schools
B. Community colleges
C. University of California buildings
D. California State University buildings
option1: A only
option2: A and B
option3: B, C and D
option4: All of the above
rationale: DSA regulates K-12 and community colleges under the Field Act[cite: 1]. UC and CSU have independent seismic boards and only use DSA for accessibility[cite: 1].

text: A General / Nationwide Permit issued by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers applies to which type of work?
option1: Projects approved on an accelerated emergency basis
option2: Projects with severe wetland displacement
option3: Projects that cause only minimal individual and cumulative adverse environmental impacts
option4: Projects with zero environmental touch
rationale: General/Nationwide permits apply to defined categories of activities that cause only minimal adverse environmental effects[cite: 1].

text: What is the primary role of the California Governor's Office of Planning and Research (OPR)?
option1: Coordinate statewide environmental review and provide CEQA guidelines
option2: Act as a binding mediator for disputes between cities
option3: Issue environmental permits for highway systems
option4: Approve architectural licenses
rationale: OPR develops CEQA implementation guidelines and runs the State Clearinghouse to coordinate state environmental reviews[cite: 1].

text: Under CEQA, what can a Responsible Agency do if it finds that a Lead Agency prepared an inadequate EIR?
option1: Nothing, the Lead Agency's decision is completely unchallengeable
option2: Request the State Clearinghouse reverse the decision
option3: Appeal to the County Grand Jury
option4: Assume the role of Lead Agency or file a legal challenge within 30 days of the NOD
rationale: CEQA Guidelines § 15096 allows a responsible agency to take over lead agency duties under certain conditions or file a court petition[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following is typically included in the civil engineer's scope of design services?
option1: Landscape irrigation design
option2: Pavement design and site parking grading/drainage
option3: Water supply pipes inside the building envelope
option4: Parking lot lighting photometrics
rationale: Civil engineers handle site grading, paving sections, and site stormwater drainage[cite: 1]. Irrigation is landscape; interior piping is plumbing; lighting is electrical[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following is NOT considered an effective internal QA/QC coordination practice?
option1: Exchanging milestone progress sets with consultants
option2: Securing written client approvals at completion of each design phase
option3: Holding the first interdisciplinary coordination meeting at the start of the CD phase
option4: Continuous senior peer review throughout the project life cycle
rationale: Waiting until the Construction Documents phase to hold the first consultant coordination meeting is far too late and leads to substantial redesign[cite: 1].

text:
Which of the following practices actively builds awareness of the standard of care and strengthens an architect's professional capability?
A. Reviewing prominent design trends
B. Studying product manufacturer technical literature
C. Attending accredited continuing education seminars
D. Participating in peer review programs
E. Publishing an article about self-projects
option1: A, B and C
option2: A, C and E
option3: A, D and E
option4: B, C and D
rationale: Manufacturer literature, continuing education courses, and peer reviews sharpen technical competency and align practice with the professional standard of care[cite: 1].

text: During Schematic Design, the Owner directs you to bypass Design Development and proceed directly to CDs to fast-track the opening. How should you respond?
option1: Comply immediately and add extra drafting staff
option2: Explain that DD is critical to resolve systems and coordinate engineering; advise of risks and explore other fast-track methods
option3: Demand that contractor shorten the construction duration instead
option4: Refuse outright and terminate the contract
rationale: Bypassing DD leads to massive coordination failures and cost overruns[cite: 1]. The architect should counsel the owner and investigate phased permitting or package bidding[cite: 1].

text: Your cost estimate shows the project is 5% over budget at the conclusion of Schematic Design. What is your contractual responsibility?
option1: Advise the client not to worry because SD estimates are approximate
option2: Tell the client to secure 5% more financing
option3: Collaborate with the client to evaluate value engineering and adjust scope or finishes to align with budget
option4: Artificially lower the square foot cost numbers on the estimate
rationale: Under AIA B101, if the architect's estimate exceeds the budget at the end of SD, the architect must review options with the owner to adjust scope, size, or quality[cite: 1].

text: Which consultant typically produces drawings that are submitted for Planning Commission design review?
option1: Civil Engineer
option2: Landscape Architect
option3: Structural Engineer
option4: Acoustical Engineer
rationale: Landscape architects prepare site layouts, hardscape, tree preservation, and planting plans which are central to planning and design review approvals[cite: 1].

text: Under AIA B101, if the Owner suspends the project for more than how many cumulative days may the Architect terminate the agreement?
option1: 30 days
option2: 60 days
option3: 90 days
option4: 120 days
rationale: AIA B101 § 9.3 allows the architect to terminate the contract upon not less than 7 days written notice if the owner suspends the project for more than 90 cumulative days[cite: 1].

text: Recessed light fixtures and grilles in suspended acoustical tile ceilings are required by California seismic codes to be supported by independent safety wires of what minimum gauge?
option1: 10 gauge
option2: 11 gauge
option3: 12 gauge
option4: 14 gauge
rationale: CISCA guidelines and ASTM standards require two 12-gauge hanger wires connected to opposite corners of recessed light fixtures[cite: 1].

text: In earthquake engineering for non-structural components, 'inertia failure' refers to damage caused by which phenomenon?
option1: Excessive shaking and accelerations acting directly on the mass of the non-structural component
option2: Building inter-story drift that distorts wall frames and glazing
option3: Differential settlement of building footings
option4: Soil liquefaction below grade
rationale: Inertia forces are proportional to the mass and seismic acceleration (F = ma), causing unrestrained heavy components to topple or break anchors[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following is NOT a design prerequisite for a base-isolated seismic structure?
option1: Superstructure designed to behave as a rigid box above the isolator plane
option2: Limiting building height/slenderness ratio to prevent overturning moments
option3: Upper levels of the building must have zero cantilevers
option4: Flexible utility connections across the seismic isolation moat
rationale: Superstructures with cantilevers are allowed provided the structure behaves rigidly as a unified diaphragm system above the isolation plane[cite: 1].

text: Under which soil or site condition is a mat (raft) foundation commonly specified?
option1: Sites with high water tables or low bearing capacity where spread footings would cover over half the footprint
option2: Sites where bedrock is shallow
option3: Steep hillside slopes prone to mudslides
option4: Dry sandy desert conditions
rationale: Mat foundations distribute loads over a massive footprint to resist differential settlement in weak soils and resist hydrostatic uplift in high water tables[cite: 1].

text: What is a major operational limitation of air-source heat pumps in cold weather conditions?
option1: Inability to provide cooling
option2: Decreased heating capacity and efficiency (COP) as outside ambient air temperatures drop
option3: High fuel storage requirements
option4: Prohibitive duct requirements
rationale: Air-source heat pumps suffer reduced coefficient of performance (COP) and diminished heating capacity in sub-freezing temperatures, requiring supplemental heat[cite: 1].

text: What is a primary distinction in water management between a curtain wall system and a storefront system?
option1: Glass color availability
option2: Operable sash hardware
option3: Curtain walls weep moisture horizontally at each story transom, while storefronts weep at the bottom sill flashing
option4: Storefronts cannot receive double glazing
rationale: Storefronts drain internal condensation to the bottom sub-sill pan; multi-story curtain walls manage water through internal gutters weeping at each floor[cite: 1].

text:
Other than cost and lead time, what criteria should architects evaluate when specifying materials?
A. Maintenance & Cleanability
B. Durability & Lifespan
C. Owner / User operational needs
D. Aesthetics
E. Whether the product is brand new and untested
option1: A, B, C and D
option2: A, B, C and E
option3: A, B, D and E
option4: B, C, D and E
rationale: Specifying untested products without proven track records violates standard risk management practices[cite: 1]. Maintenance, durability, user need, and aesthetics are standard[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following items is typically shown on detail sections and wall details rather than on roof plans?
option1: Roof crickets
option2: Continuous thermal insulation layers
option3: Roof drain locations
option4: Rooftop mechanical equipment
rationale: Insulation thickness, vapor retarders, and attachment details are detailed in wall/roof sections; roof plans show geometry, drains, crickets, and curbs[cite: 1].

text: Which dimensional data is typically found directly on drawing schedules rather than in project specifications?
option1: Ceiling tile sizes
option2: Door and window frame sizes
option3: Plumbing fixture diameters
option4: Stud gauge thicknesses
rationale: Door and window sizes and opening schedules belong on drawings; material technical performance and standards belong in specs[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following documents does NOT exist at the time the original bidding documents are issued?
option1: Form of Agreement
option2: General and Supplementary Conditions
option3: Bonding Requirements
option4: Addenda
rationale: Addenda are modifications issued during the bidding period prior to bid receipt; they do not exist when the initial bid set is issued[cite: 1].

text: Plan check returns with major spatial conflicts between mechanical duct runs and structural beams. What is your first action?
option1: Notify the owner that the permit is failed
option2: Redesign the ductwork yourself without engineering input
option3: Review the comments and convene an immediate coordination meeting with the mechanical and structural engineers
option4: Instruct the consultants to work it out without architect participation
rationale: The architect in responsible control leads coordination between structural and MEP disciplines to resolve spatial clashes[cite: 1].

text: If the Owner engages a Construction Manager as Advisor (CMa), which architectural CA service is shared or significantly filtered?
option1: Review and certification of contractor payment applications
option2: Issuance of architectural sketches
option3: Final building occupancy inspection
option4: Conducting aesthetic punch lists
rationale: Under AIA C132/A232, the Construction Manager reviews and certifies the contractor's payment application before passing it to the architect for joint approval[cite: 1].

text: What is the registered Architect's legal responsibility regarding Special Inspections under Chapter 17 of the CBC?
option1: Prepare and submit the Statement of Special Inspections to the building official
option2: Directly hire and compensate the special inspectors
option3: Perform all destructive laboratory testing personally
option4: Guarantee that the contractor's work is defect-free
rationale: The registered design professional prepares and submits the schedule/statement of special inspections to the building official[cite: 1].

text: In a construction surety performance or payment bond, who is the 'Principal'?
option1: The Architect
option2: The Owner (Obligee)
option3: The General Contractor
option4: The Bonding Surety Company
rationale: In surety bonding, the Contractor is the Principal (whose performance is guaranteed), the Owner is the Obligee, and the insurance carrier is the Surety[cite: 1].

text: Which of the following is a primary characteristic of private binding arbitration compared to courtroom litigation?
option1: Arbitration decisions can easily be appealed on legal errors
option2: Arbitration proceedings are confidential and private
option3: Arbitration is governed by strict public judicial rules of evidence
option4: Arbitration is open to public court reporters
rationale: Arbitration proceedings and awards are private and confidential, and grounds for judicial appeal are very limited[cite: 1].

text: In a construction contract, what is the definition of 'Liquidated Damages'?
option1: A punitive fine assessed against the contractor for poor workmanship
option2: A penalty imposed on the owner for late progress payments
option3: A pre-agreed reasonable estimate of daily financial loss incurred by the owner if construction is delayed past Substantial Completion
option4: Compensation paid to subcontractors when work is shut down
rationale: Liquidated damages are a predetermined daily sum intended to compensate the owner for actual financial loss resulting from late completion (not a punitive penalty)[cite: 1].

text:
Which of the following are recognized contract documents used to modify the construction work?
A. Bulletins
B. Change Orders
C. Construction Change Directives (CCD)
D. Orders for a Minor Change in the Work (ASI)
option1: A, B and C
option2: A, B and D
option3: A, C and D
option4: B, C and D
rationale: AIA A201 explicitly defines Change Orders, CCDs, and Architect's Orders for a Minor Change[cite: 1]. 'Bulletin' is an informal term, not a contract modification document[cite: 1].

text: Under AIA Document A201, how many days does the Architect have after receipt of the Contractor's Application for Payment to either certify or withhold payment?
option1: 5 days
option2: 7 days
option3: 10 days
option4: 14 days
rationale: AIA A201 § 9.4.1 requires the architect to either issue a Certificate for Payment or state reasons for withholding within 7 days[cite: 1].

text: Under AIA A201 § 14.1, which of the following is a valid ground for the Contractor to terminate the contract?
option1: The work is suspended by the Owner for 10 days
option2: Work is stopped for 30 consecutive days under an act of government or court order through no fault of the Contractor
option3: The Architect takes 8 days to review an RFI
option4: A subcontractor goes out of business
rationale: The contractor may terminate the contract if the work is stopped for 30 consecutive days by government order or court injunction through no fault of the contractor[cite: 1].

text:
Which of the following must the Contractor submit to the Architect to receive Final Payment?
A. Contractor's affidavit of payment of debts and claims (AIA G706)
B. Consent of Surety to Final Payment (AIA G707)
C. Final unconditional lien waivers and releases
D. Building occupancy permit
option1: A, B and C
option2: A, B and D
option3: A, C and D
option4: B, C and D
rationale: G706, G707, and lien waivers are required closeout submittals for final payment[cite: 1]. The certificate of occupancy is issued by the building official to the owner[cite: 1].

text: Under California Government Code § 65583, which state agency is tasked with reviewing local municipal General Plan Housing Elements for statutory compliance with the Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA)?
option1: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD)
option2: Governor's Office of Planning and Research (OPR)
option3: California Department of Real Estate (DRE)
option4: California Department of Consumer Affairs (DCA)
rationale: California Government Code § 65583 requires local jurisdictions to submit draft Housing Elements to the Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) for certification and RHNA compliance review.

text: A city fails to adopt an HCD-compliant Housing Element by the statutory deadline. Under California Housing Element Law, what automatic consequence may a developer invoke for a project providing 20% low-income housing?
option1: The Builder's Remedy, which restricts the municipality's authority to deny the project based on local zoning or general plan inconsistencies
option2: Automatic issuance of a building permit without plan check review
option3: Exemption from all CBC Title 24 Building Standards and fire marshal approvals
option4: Automatic entitlement of a 100% density bonus and full waiver of all development impact fees
rationale: Under the Housing Accountability Act (Gov. Code § 65589.5), the 'Builder's Remedy' restricts non-compliant municipalities from denying qualifying affordable housing projects on the basis of general plan or zoning non-conformance.

text: Under BPC § 5536.22, which of the following contract provisions is an explicit statutory requirement for an architect entering into a written agreement with a client in California?
option1: A statement notifying the client that the architect is licensed by the California Architects Board
option2: A mandatory binding arbitration clause naming the American Arbitration Association (AAA)
option3: An express limitation of liability clause capping damages at the architect's professional fee
option4: A statutory warranty certifying that the completed project will conform with the client's initial budget
rationale: BPC § 5536.22(a)(5) requires that all written contracts include a statement informing the client that architects are licensed and regulated by the California Architects Board, including CAB contact details.

text: An architect is hired by a corporate client to provide schematic feasibility studies on an hourly basis. Under BPC § 5536.22, under what condition is a written contract legally NOT required?
option1: When the client is a public agency or when professional services are rendered without compensation to the architect
option2: Whenever services are billed at an hourly rate rather than a stipulated lump sum
option3: Whenever the total anticipated fee is estimated to be less than $10,000
option4: If the client provides an oral promise to sign an agreement prior to permit submittal
rationale: BPC § 5536.22(b) exempts an architect from the written agreement mandate only if: (1) professional services are rendered for free, (2) the client is a public agency, (3) the client signs a pre-existing master service agreement, or (4) services are of the same general kind previously rendered to and paid for by the client.

text: An architect forms a professional corporation in California to offer architectural services. Pursuant to the Moscone-Knox Professional Corporation Act and CAB regulations, what minimum percentage of voting shares must be owned by licensed design professionals?
option1: 100% of the shares must be owned by licensed persons, with licensed architects owning at least 51%
option2: At least 51% must be owned by licensed architects, while the remaining 49% may be owned by unlicensed investors
option3: At least 75% of shares must be owned by licensed architects, with 25% owned by staff employees
option4: A minimum of 50% must be owned by architects, with no restriction on non-professional owners
rationale: Under the Moscone-Knox Professional Corporation Act (Corp. Code § 13401.5) and CAB rules, non-licensed individuals cannot hold voting shares; 100% must be held by licensed design professionals, and licensed architects must own at least 51%.

text: Under California law, an architect's legal standard of care requires that the architect exercise:
option1: The degree of skill and care ordinarily exercised by reasonably prudent architects practicing under similar circumstances in the same locality
option2: The highest level of technical perfection and strict adherence to zero-defect construction
option3: Guaranteed compliance with all building code interpretations subsequently made by the plan checker
option4: The standard of care defined by published national AIA guidelines, irrespective of local jurisdictional practice
rationale: In California, common law establishes the architect's standard of care as the degree of learning and skill ordinarily possessed by reputable professionals practicing in the same or similar locality under similar circumstances.

text: An architect is sued for breach of contract and negligence. Under California Business and Professions Code § 5588, within how many days must an architect report a civil judgment or settlement exceeding $5,000 against them to the California Architects Board?
option1: Within 30 days of the settlement, judgment, or arbitration award
option2: Within 10 days of service of the summons and complaint
option3: Within 60 days following the conclusion of the calendar year
option4: Only during the biennial license renewal filing
rationale: BPC § 5588 mandates that a licensee report any settlement or arbitration award of $5,000 or greater resulting from professional negligence or breach of contract to the California Architects Board in writing within 30 days.

text: Which document, prepared by a regional Council of Governments (COG) in coordination with HCD, establishes the minimum housing production allocation that local municipal general plans must accommodate?
option1: Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA)
option2: California Environmental Quality Act Initial Study (IS)
option3: Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR)
option4: Capital Improvement Program (CIP)
rationale: HCD allocates regional housing targets to regional planning councils (such as SCAG or ABAG), which distribute the Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA) to cities and counties for inclusion in their General Plan Housing Elements.

text: An architect prepares project feasibility budgets for a commercial project. In California, which project cost component represents a municipal impact fee levied under the Mitigation Fee Act (Gov. Code § 66000)?
option1: A development impact fee established to offset the capital cost of public infrastructure improvements caused by the project
option2: A mandatory fee paid to the California Architects Board upon building permit submittal
option3: An administrative penalty levied by the Regional Water Quality Control Board for stormwater compliance
option4: A local building department surcharge dedicated entirely to third-party accessibility review
rationale: The Mitigation Fee Act (AB 1600, Gov. Code § 66000) governs the establishment and collection of local development impact fees charged to defray the cost of public facilities necessitated by new development.

text: Under the California Density Bonus Law (Gov. Code § 65915), a residential development project providing 10% lower-income units is entitled to which of the following statutory benefits?
option1: A density bonus percentage and at least one development incentive or concession
option2: A total exemption from CEQA environmental review and coastal development permits
option3: Full waiver of all building code structural requirements under CBC Chapter 16
option4: Automatic rezoning of the parcel from commercial to heavy industrial
rationale: Government Code § 65915 entitles developers who dedicate specified percentages of affordable units to a base density bonus, reduced parking requirements, and statutory incentives or concessions that reduce site development standards.

text: An architect includes a clause in a residential design contract stating: 'Architect shall be held harmless from any and all liability, including damages resulting from Architect's sole gross negligence or intentional misconduct.' Under California Civil Code § 1668, what is the legal validity of this clause?
option1: It is void and unenforceable as against public policy
option2: It is fully enforceable if the client signs an initialed separate waiver
option3: It is enforceable only if professional liability insurance limits are stated in the contract
option4: It is valid for single-family residential projects but void for multi-family commercial projects
rationale: California Civil Code § 1668 establishes that contracts which have for their object to exempt anyone from responsibility for his own fraud, willful injury to the person or property of another, or violation of law, whether willful or negligent, are against public policy and void.

text: In California, an architectural firm operating as a Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) must register with which two state entities prior to offering professional services?
option1: The California Secretary of State and the California Architects Board
option2: The Department of Housing and Community Development and the State Clearinghouse
option3: The California Department of Tax and Fee Administration and Cal/OSHA
option4: The Governor's Office of Planning and Research and the Department of Consumer Affairs
rationale: An architectural LLP must be registered with the California Secretary of State pursuant to the Corporations Code and hold a Certificate of Registration from the California Architects Board (BPC § 5580).

text: Under BPC § 5536.22, if an architect provides additional services outside the original contract scope on an hourly basis, how must these additional services be documented to comply with the Practice Act?
option1: Through a written amendment describing the additional services and compensation basis, executed before or promptly upon commencing the work
option2: By billing the additional hours directly on the next monthly invoice without prior client authorization
option3: Through an oral agreement between the project manager and contractor recorded in job meeting minutes
option4: No documentation is required as long as the base contract explicitly references standard AIA G802 forms
rationale: BPC § 5536.22 requires that changes in the professional services provided or compensation to be paid must be memorialized in a written amendment executed by both parties.

text: What is the primary role of the Governor's Office of Planning and Research (OPR) in California project development?
option1: Formulating state planning priorities, maintaining the CEQA Guidelines, and operating the State Clearinghouse
option2: Directly reviewing architectural construction documents for structural safety and Title 24 access
option3: Issuing Coastal Development Permits for projects located along certified shoreline segments
option4: Enforcing the California Architects Practice Act and prosecuting unlicensed practice violations
